entries.1:1: The writer, a church leader, greets a Christian woman and her children whom God has chosen, and says he truly loves them, as do all who know the truth. It shows that real love grows among people who share faith in the truth.
entries.1:2: This love is based on the truth that lives in us and will stay with us forever. What you believe is not temporary; it stays with you for good.
entries.1:3: He wishes them grace, mercy, and peace from God the Father and from Jesus Christ, his Son, joined with true love. These good gifts come from God and from Jesus together.
entries.1:4: He was very glad to find some of her children living the right way, just as God the Father commanded. It is a joy to see people actually living out what they have been taught.
entries.1:5: He asks her, not for some new rule, but for the command they had from the beginning: that we love one another. Loving each other is not a new idea but the heart of the faith from the start.
entries.1:6: Love means doing what God commands, and this command to love was given from the beginning. Real love shows itself in obeying God, not just in feelings.
entries.1:7: Many false teachers have gone out who deny that Jesus Christ came as a real human being. Anyone who denies this is a deceiver and opposed to Christ.
entries.1:8: Watch out so you don't lose what has been worked for, but receive your full reward. Be careful to hold on to the truth so your effort is not wasted.
entries.1:9: Anyone who runs ahead and does not stay with Christ's teaching does not have God, but whoever stays with the teaching has both the Father and the Son. Staying faithful to what Jesus taught keeps you close to God.
entries.1:10: If someone comes to you without this teaching, don't welcome him into your house or encourage him. Showing hospitality to a false teacher can give support to his wrong message.
entries.1:11: Anyone who welcomes such a person shares in his evil work. Encouraging a false teacher makes you a partner in what he is doing.
entries.1:12: He has much more to say but doesn't want to write it all with paper and ink; he hopes to visit and talk face to face so their joy will be complete. Some things are better said in person than in a letter.
entries.1:13: The children of her chosen sister send their greetings. Fellow believers, pictured as family, pass on their love to her.
